stage_model.description: A named, versioned stage-gate process. Several portfolios may follow one model; a new version is a new model, so programs in flight keep the one they started on.

stage.description: One stage or gate of a stage model. Codes are unique within a model only: 'LO' in small-molecule discovery and 'LO' in biologics discovery are different rows.

ordinal.description: Position in the model; advancing moves to the next ordinal

phase.description: Grouping of stages, e.g. a CMC phase

is_gate.description: Entering this stage is a governed decision

is_terminal.description: Leaving the model from here hands the program on to another portfolio

governance.description: Who decides, e.g. a gate review board

aliases.description: Unused: string_list values cannot be written from JS today (Types.fromValue reports a JS array as 'list'); see spellings

spellings.description: Other spellings a registry feed may use for this stage, separated by |

folders.description: Folders the workspace builder adds under a program's folder once it reaches this stage: '/'-separated paths, '|' between them

gate_criterion.description: What must hold to enter a stage.

rule.description: For data conditions: the rule as a person reads it

condition.description: For data conditions: the rule as the portal evaluates it over the program dataset (scope, where, measured, minCount). Without it the criterion is recorded by hand

modality.description: Applies only to programs of this modality (matches program.modality); empty = every modality

artifact.description: What the criterion rests on: model_run = a run saved to the program is chosen for it from the gate panel

run_filter.description: Which of the program's runs the criterion offers: unitOperations, runTypes, models (catalogue codes); empty = every run

portfolio.description: The unit of configuration: one registry, one stage model, one set of access groups, one workspace root.

stage_authority.description: feed: the registry owns the stage and the portal mirrors it; portal: gate decisions are made and recorded here

program_noun.description: What this portfolio calls a program: Project, Program, Molecule

workspace_root.description: Name of the root space the workspace builder creates the portfolio's tree under

workstreams.description: Folders the builder creates under every program, '|'-separated (Chemistry|Biology|DMPK)

flow_folders.description: Unit-operation folders from each program's process flows, off when empty: {placement: process_type|program, fromStage, flows: [{code, name, processType, steps: [{step, unitOperation, folderName}]}], rules: [{modality, flow, priority}]}. program_flow rows win for their process type

work_units.description: Work units the portfolio uses, '|'-separated: campaign, series, study, process_stage

program_data.description: The program dataset query data conditions are evaluated over: connection, sql with @program, leadRoles

program_datasets.description: Further datasets of every program, the program page opens each: {datasets: [{code, name, connection, sql with @program, viewers}]}

attention.description: Rules over the program dataset that flag compounds or lots needing attention: {rules: [{code, name, severity, condition, message}]}

schedule.description: When syncDuePortfolios syncs it: an interval (every 6h) or a five-field cron line in UTC (0 6 * * 1-5); empty = only on call

owners.description: User logins told about a scheduled sync that changed something, '|'-separated

handoff.description: Where a program goes when it leaves the terminal stage: {to: portfolio code, fromStage: stage code}

auto_advance.description: Stage advance driven by data, off when empty: {through: stage code, countWaivers}. Portal authority only

dmta.description: DMTA status sources (F-24), optional: {tested: {dataset, compoundColumn, dateColumn}, sources: [Package:Function]}

personas.description: Quick actions per persona: {default, groups: [{group, persona}], cards: {persona: [action code or {name, function, description}]}}

document_kinds.description: The portfolio's document vocabulary: {kinds: [{code, name, description}]}. Empty: one kind per document criterion, and other

approval.description: Optional approval workflow (F-30), off when empty: {decisions: [advance, terminate, ...], artifacts: [document, model_card], approvers: N}. A decision or artifact of a listed kind is proposed, and takes effect once N approvers other than the proposer approve

ask_sme.description: Optional Ask SME channel (F-51): {channel: discussion | group | user | external, group, users: [login], external: {kind, address}, note}. The question always goes into the program's discussion (the platform chat on its folder); the channel picks who is told in the platform. Default: the portfolio's approvers. external is not wired

registry_feed.description: A query that yields this portfolio's programs. Two portfolios may read the same source system; their feeds must partition it (see the routing audit).

system.description: The source system; programs from the same system with the same key are the same thing

connection.description: Data connection name, resolved on the server at sync time

target.description: What the feed delivers: programs, one kind of work unit, or compounds in programs, keyed by program code

mapping.description: Feed column → program field, plus status and stage value maps

program.description: A program (project) of one portfolio. Private by default; sync shares it with its portfolio's groups.

sourced_has_ref.message: A synced program needs its registry reference

stage_model_id.description: Copied from the portfolio at creation; a model upgrade does not move programs in flight

source_stage.description: The stage exactly as the registry spelled it

external_ref.description: <system>:<key> — the program's identity in its source system

predecessor_id.description: The program in another portfolio this one continues (e.g. discovery → CMC)

space_id.description: The program's folder in its portfolio workspace, recorded by the builder so a renamed program keeps its folder

details.description: Registry columns the portfolio does not map

stage_transition.description: The gate log: every stage change of a program, who made it and why. Written once.

source.description: Who moved the program: an approver in the app, the registry seen by a sync, or the program's data (auto-advance); empty on rows written before 0.2.12

evidence.description: What the data said when the program advanced by data: each required criterion and its result

outcome.description: The outcome of a recorded decision (decision record): a gate decision recorded in the app where the registry owns the stage; empty on other rows

criterion_status.description: A program's instance of one gate criterion, of any kind. The development profile calls document-kind instances Deliverables.

status.description: Data conditions use only met and not_met

document.description: The document that satisfies a document criterion, e.g. the CoA

evidence.description: Notes: what satisfies the criterion, or why it was waived

campaign.description: Iterative and open-ended work under a program: a screen, a hit triage, a DMTA cycle. Success is a state it reaches (outcome), not a completion.

outcome.description: What the campaign reached; an open campaign may still succeed

missing_from_feed.description: Its feed no longer delivers it; kept, never deleted

details.description: Feed columns the work unit does not map

series.description: A chemical series of a program: compounds sharing a scaffold. A work unit, never a folder of compounds (FR-26).

maturity.description: The portfolio's series maturity vocabulary, e.g. hit, validated, lead, optimized, candidate

missing_from_feed.description: Its feed no longer delivers it; kept, never deleted

details.description: Feed columns the work unit does not map

study.description: Designed, closed-ended work under a program: an in vivo PK study, a tox study, a stability study. Success is completion.

type.description: e.g. in vivo PK, efficacy, toxicology, stability

missing_from_feed.description: Its feed no longer delivers it; kept, never deleted

details.description: Feed columns the work unit does not map

process_stage.description: A stage of a program's manufacturing process, e.g. upstream, purification, formulation.

missing_from_feed.description: Its feed no longer delivers it; kept, never deleted

details.description: Feed columns the work unit does not map

compound.description: The identity of a registry compound (system and code), so programs can share it. Its name, structure, aliases and batches live on program_compound, under each program's security: this table was readable by every user, so loading a portfolio takes All users View away and moveToSecuredTables copies the values to the links and empties them here. The portal never mints a compound and never promotes one.

system.description: The registry the code belongs to

details.description: Registry columns the portal does not map

program_compound.description: A compound in a program, with its role there. Many-to-many: a tool compound serves several programs. Every role change is logged in compound_role_change.

compound_code.description: The compound's registration code, copied from compound so a reader of the program needs no access to the compound table

smiles.description: The structure, as the portfolio's registry gives it

details.description: Registry columns the portal does not map

compound_role_change.description: The history of a compound's role in a program: who changed it, when, why. Written once.

unit_operation.description: Global catalogue of process operations, not per flow: Thaw appears in several flows and has one definition, so runs and recommendations point at the operation.

ordinal.description: Typical process order, for display outside any one flow

portfolios.description: Codes of the portfolios whose catalogue declares it, '|'-separated; what exportPortfolio writes back

run_type.description: How a run was executed (physical, simulated, digital twin, ...). A table rather than choices because the definitions are the content and a profile adds values without a redeploy.

portfolios.description: Codes of the portfolios whose catalogue declares it, '|'-separated; what exportPortfolio writes back

is_execution_mode.description: False for values on another axis (input provenance, a run's role) that are not mutually exclusive execution modes

process_flow.description: A manufacturing flow: an ordered list of unit operations (process_step).

process_type.description: The profile's split of flows, e.g. Drug Substance / Drug Product. A program runs one flow per process type.

process_step.description: A unit operation at a position in a flow. The workspace tree's leaf level is built from these.

folder_name.description: Numbered folder label, e.g. '05 - ProA Affinity Chromatography'

branch_group.description: Steps sharing a value are parallel branches

flow_rule.description: Which flows a program runs, by modality. Resolved at sync into program_flow: one winner per process type, highest priority first.

priority.description: Higher wins within a process type

program_flow.description: The flows a program runs. Sync writes rule rows from flow_rule; a manual row overrides the rules for its process type and sync leaves it alone.

model.description: Catalogue of models: one identity per model across name variants and versions.

code.description: Func nqName: the stable handle, since Func ids change every package release

current_version.description: The model version in use; its model_card is the current card

portfolios.description: Codes of the portfolios whose catalogue declares the model, '|'-separated; the save-to-program dialog offers the first one

unit_operations.description: Codes of the unit operations the model applies to, '|'-separated; the first is the default when a run is saved

default_run_type_id.description: How a run of the model is usually executed (simulated, digital twin, ...)

model_card.description: What a version of a model is for, written around the scientific question it answers (FR-50, PORT-41, PORT-43). One card per model version; an older version's card stays as lineage.

model_version.description: The model version the card describes

question.description: The scientific question the model answers

intended_use.description: What the model is for, and what it is not for

inputs.description: The inputs as {params: [...]}: name, caption, units, and the validity range (min, max) the model was built for

outputs.description: The outputs as {params: [...]}: name, caption, units

applicability.description: The applicability domain in words: the processes, modalities, scales it holds for

performance.description: How well it predicts, and against what data

lineage.description: What it was built from: data, method, the version it replaces

supersedes.description: The model version this one replaces

owner.description: The person or team who answers for the model

approval.description: in_review while an approval request is pending (F-30); rejected when an approver turned it down

applies_to.description: Where the model applies, for recommendation: {tasks, stages, modalities, workUnits, predicts, rank}; a key left out matches anything

model_run.description: Curated projection over a saved FuncCall: one row per scientifically meaningful run, not per invocation.

func_call.description: The saved FuncCall. A soft reference: it may dangle if the call is hard-deleted, which model_name keeps readable. Empty while the platform refuses the soft reference (soft-ref alias bug); run_id holds the id then

run_id.description: The saved FuncCall's id as plain text, always written. Migration debt: the fallback while func_call cannot be written; once it can, func_call is backfilled from it

model_name.description: Func nqName as run, kept because a run is a historical record

stage_id.description: The program's stage when the run was saved. Written once.

purpose.description: Why the run was done; orthogonal to how (run type)

sync_run.description: Superseded by sync_log (0.3.0), which secures each row; kept for history. Every user could read it, so loading a portfolio takes All users View away and moveToSecuredTables copies its rows to sync_log.

created.description: Programs, work units, compounds and compound links created

updated.description: Programs, work units, compounds and roles changed, and rows back in their feed

flagged.description: Programs, work units and compound links flagged in this run as no longer in their feed

unresolved.description: Stage spellings that resolved to no stage

error.description: Why the run stopped; empty when it finished

summary.description: The run's report, as syncPortfolio returns it

changes.description: Per-program changes, standing overlaps and what followers were told: {programs: [{program, created, fields, stage, missing, units, compounds, advanced}], overlaps: [...], newData: [{program, line}]}

notified.description: Who was told about the run, or why nobody was

criterion_artifact.description: Which runs were considered for a criterion, and which one the team chose. Selection instead of approval. Carries program_id because master security delegates one hop only.

rationale.description: Why this run over the others

follow.description: Superseded by following (0.3.0), which only its user reads; kept for history. Every user could read everyone's follows, so loading a portfolio takes All users View, Edit and Delete away. Rows are not copied: the server makes the caller a row's author, so a copy would belong to whoever copied it.

work_unit_kind.description: Empty when the whole program is followed

work_unit_code.description: The work unit's code, e.g. the series

active.description: False once unfollowed; following again turns it back on. Kept instead of deleted: the server refuses to delete a row of a table without soft delete

checked.description: The data as last checked for news: {rows, values, mark}

news_on.description: When last_news was told; the activity feed shows it

seen.description: The data at the user's last visit to the program page: {rows, values, mark}

program_role.description: Viewers, contributors and approvers of one program, on top of the portfolio's groups. Managed by the portfolio's approvers in the app; the server lets only the portfolios' approvers groups write it (Edit granted when a portfolio is loaded); drives the program's workspace folder grants, and its row grants once GROK-21041 is fixed.

group_id.description: A group, or a user's personal group

active.description: False once the role is removed; giving a role again turns it back on

evidence.description: What a gate decision rested on: a model run, a program snapshot, a file, a URL, or a criterion's state at the gate. The target is a soft reference (its id or address as text, no foreign key) with its name and context frozen when attached, so the evidence reads the same after the target is renamed or deleted. Written once.

stage_transition_id.description: The gate-log entry the evidence supports

target.description: Soft reference: a run's run_id, a snapshot's id, a file path, a URL, or a gate criterion's id

name.description: The target's name when attached, frozen

role.description: readiness: a criterion as the gate saw it; supporting: attached by the decider

context.description: What the target said when attached: a run's model and selection, a criterion's state and data summary

program_snapshot.description: A program frozen at one time (FR-15): stage, status, the state of each criterion, the runs selected, and the program dataset as a CSV file in the program's workspace folder, fingerprinted by its SHA-256. Written once; a decision may take one as evidence.

note.description: Why it was taken, or why its table was not kept

stage_code.description: The program's stage then, frozen; empty when unstaged

criteria.description: Every criterion that applies: stage, code, name, required, state, basis, what the data said

artifacts.description: The run selected for each criterion: run_id, title, model, who chose it and why

table_folder.description: The space holding the table file: the program's workspace folder

table_file.description: The CSV file's name in that folder; empty when the table was not kept

table_sha256.description: SHA-256 of the CSV as written, so a changed file is noticed

document.description: A document over a file (F-27): in the program's workspace folder or at any file path. Its kind comes from the portfolio's vocabulary; it may answer one gate criterion of kind document, which is met when the document is approved, unless waived. A newer approved version supersedes the older.

status.description: submitted while an approval request is pending, rejected when an approver turned it down (portfolios with an approval workflow, F-30)

path.description: The file's full path as the platform reads it: System:AppData/..., or a space file Space:Program:Files/name

folder.description: The program's workspace folder (space id) when the file is in it

generated.description: An evidence table generated by the portal (F-40): the criterion, when and by whom, the evidence it was generated from (each source with a content hash, and one hash over all), the CSV beside it. Empty for a document a person wrote

evidence_check.description: The last check of a generated document against the evidence now (F-41): current or stale, the evidence hash now, what changed, when, and the hash its author and followers were last told about

prediction.description: What a version of a catalogued predictive model said about one compound of a program (F-22, FR-58): one value per compound and predicted program-data column, from a batch scoring that is saved as a model run. Written once per model version; scoring the same version again keeps what is stored.

compound_id.description: The registry compound, when the code is one

compound_code.description: The compound as the program dataset names it

model_code.description: The model's catalogue code (func nqName), kept because a prediction is a historical record

model_version.description: The card version the model ran as

predicts.description: The program-data column the value stands in for, from the card's appliesTo.predicts

model_run_id.description: The scoring run; removing the run removes its predictions

run_id.description: The saved call's id, as on model_run

approval_request.description: Superseded by approval (0.3.0), which secures each row; kept for history. Every user could read it, so loading a portfolio takes All users View away (a redeploy never revokes a grant) and moveToSecuredTables copies its rows to approval.

to_stage_id.description: The stage an advance or recycle goes to, as proposed

target.description: Soft reference: the document's or the model card's id

title.description: What is proposed, in one line

source.description: Who proposed it: a person, or the program's data (auto-advance), which any approver may then approve

evidence.description: What the decision rests on, as proposed: {items: [...], text}

result.description: What approving did (the decision recorded, the document approved), or why it could not

stage_transition_id.description: The gate-log entry the approved decision wrote

parked_folder.description: A workspace folder moved out of the way (FR-22): a root folder no program claims, or the folder of a program that ended, moved into _Parked/<date> under the portfolio's root. Never deleted; unparking moves it back. Written by parkOrphans and unparkFolder, which check that the user is one of the portfolio's approvers; the server lets only the portfolios' approvers groups write it.

space_id.description: The folder's space id; a move keeps it

kind.description: unclaimed: no program claims it; park: its program ended or left its feed

from_parent_id.description: The space it was moved out of: the portfolio's root

parked_in_id.description: The _Parked/<date> space it was moved into

observation.description: A curated conclusion on a program, series, compound, campaign or study (F-26, FR-76/106): a title, the finding, who and when, and the evidence it rests on. Kept when retracted, with who, when and why. Written by addObservation and retractObservation, which check that the user is one of the program's contributors or approvers.

subject_code.description: The work unit's or compound's code; empty for the program itself

finding.description: The conclusion, in the author's words

evidence.description: What it rests on: {items: [{kind, target, name}]} (a run's run_id, a snapshot's id, a file path, a URL), names frozen when written

design_set.description: Compounds proposed for a series (F-23, FR-101): enumerated, generated or drawn by hand, each scored and ranked, and the ones chosen for synthesis marked. The proposals are design_proposal rows.

series_code.description: The series of the program the designs extend

score_name.description: What the score is, e.g. predicted pIC50

higher_is_better.description: Rank by score descending; false ranks ascending

design_proposal.description: One proposed compound of a design set: its structure, score and rank, and whether it was chosen for synthesis, by whom and when. Once registered, the compound's code.

label.description: The proposal's name within its set, e.g. KIN-A-D07

rank.description: 1 is best; ties share a rank

chosen_by.description: Who last chose or unchose it

chosen_on.description: When it was last chosen or unchosen

selection_set.description: A hit list (F-23, FR-102): compounds picked from a campaign, with the rationale and who picked them.

campaign_code.description: The campaign the compounds were picked from

approval.description: Approval requests, secured per row (replaces approval_request, which every user could read). A row is linked into its program's workspace folder, or into the portfolio's root for a model card, so the portfolio's groups and the program's roles see it (View only) and nobody else does. The proposer reaches their own row. No group holds View on the table; the portfolios' contributors groups hold Edit (granted when a portfolio is loaded), which lets them write any row: which contributor may review which request is the app's check.

to_stage_id.description: The stage an advance or recycle goes to, as proposed

target.description: Soft reference: the document's or the model card's id

title.description: What is proposed, in one line

source.description: Who proposed it: a person, or the program's data (auto-advance), which any approver may then approve

evidence.description: What the decision rests on, as proposed: {items: [...], text}

result.description: What approving did (the decision recorded, the document approved), or why it could not

stage_transition_id.description: The gate-log entry the approved decision wrote

sync_log.description: Sync runs, secured per row (replaces sync_run, which every user could read). A row is linked into its portfolio's workspace root, so only the portfolio's groups see it (View only). The portfolios' approvers groups hold Edit on the table, granted when a portfolio is loaded.

created.description: Programs, work units, compounds and compound links created

updated.description: Programs, work units, compounds and roles changed, and rows back in their feed

flagged.description: Programs, work units and compound links flagged in this run as no longer in their feed

unresolved.description: Stage spellings that resolved to no stage

error.description: Why the run stopped; empty when it finished

summary.description: The run's report, as syncPortfolio returns it

changes.description: Per-program changes, standing overlaps and what followers were told: {programs: [{program, created, fields, stage, missing, units, compounds, advanced}], overlaps: [...], newData: [{program, line}], folders: [program code]: the programs that got a workspace folder}

notified.description: Who was told about the run, or why nobody was

following.description: Follows, private to their user (replaces follow, which every user could read). Row security with no grants on rows: each user reaches only the rows they wrote; admins reach all, so an admin's sync updates every follower's news. All users hold View, Edit and Delete on the table, which with defaultRowVisibility none opens no one else's row.

work_unit_kind.description: Empty when the whole program is followed

work_unit_code.description: The work unit's code, e.g. the series

active.description: False once unfollowed; following again turns it back on

checked.description: The data as last checked for news: {rows, values, mark}

news_on.description: When last_news was told; the activity feed shows it

seen.description: The data at the user's last visit to the program page: {rows, values, mark}
